intervals.label: SNOLAB operating (expansion of SNO)
intervals.note: SNOLAB's own April 2011 update page says the last area of the laboratory was opened for occupancy in March 2011, so that the entire lab operates as a clean lab. This is the date the full expanded laboratory came into use; SNOLAB's earlier history as the SNO cavern (and the opening of parts of the laboratory before March 2011) is not dated here, so the facility's start is approximate.
intervals.quote: The last area of the laboratory has now been given the “clean” designation and was opened for occupancy in March 2011. This means the entire lab is operating as a clean lab

name: SNOLAB
notes: No official page consulted gives a numeric m.w.e. (metres water equivalent) shielding figure or a founding year distinct from the SNO legacy; both are left unrecorded rather than guessed. The commonly quoted '6010 m.w.e.' figure could not be re-confirmed on an official page and is therefore NOT recorded.

The operating-start date (March 2011) is the date SNOLAB's own April 2011 update page gives for the last area of the laboratory being opened, so that the entire lab operates as a clean lab (archived copy); it marks the full expanded laboratory, not the earlier SNO cavern, and is marked approximate.

operator_text.quote: Oversight and governance of the SNOLAB facility and the operational management is through the SNOLAB Institute Board of Directors, whose member institutions are Carleton University, Laurentian University, Queen’s University, University of Alberta and the Université de Montréal.
operator_text.value: SNOLAB Institute (governed by a Board of Directors whose member institutions are Carleton University, Laurentian University, Queen's University, University of Alberta and the Université de Montréal)

summary.plain: A deep underground physics laboratory two kilometres below the surface in an active nickel mine near Sudbury, Canada. The thick rock overhead blocks nearly all cosmic rays, letting scientists search for dark matter and study neutrinos in an extremely quiet environment.
summary.technical: Class-2000 clean-room underground laboratory at the 6800 ft level (~2070 m rock overburden) of Vale's Creighton nickel mine near Sudbury, Ontario, reached via 9 Shaft; an expansion of the original SNO cavern, governed by a consortium of five Canadian universities.
